card.name: Chakacha
card.tagline: Swahili coastal women's hip-driven wedding dance
card.profile: Chakacha is a traditional music and dance style (a ngoma) of the Swahili people of coastal Kenya and Tanzania, originally associated with weddings and traditionally performed and watched by women (Wikipedia). The hip-swaying movement, danced with a belt tied at the waist for ease of movement, bears resemblance to Middle Eastern belly dance, reflecting centuries of Arab and Persian trade influence on the Swahili coast. It shares music and Swahili lyrics with taarab and uses a twelve-beat triplet rhythm.
card.insight: In the late 20th century bands such as Mombasa Roots, Safari Sound Band and Them Mushrooms adapted chakacha into popular Afropop, carrying the once women-only wedding genre onto commercial recordings (Wikipedia).
